["The weather is starting to get cooler, and it's that time of year for camping and tailgating before American football games. The BLAVOR 20000mAh Solar Charger is designed for this very occasion. It has four built-in charging cables, so you don't need to bring any cables with you; it comes with a solar panel for supplemental power; and there's even a wireless charging pad on top for your iPhone and Apple Watch. Let's take a look."]

['MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers brings you the latest products in the MagSafe and wireless charging space, helping you get the most out of your wireless charging-compatible Apple devices.']

['Four built-in charging cables']

['This design is the most appealing part of the entire product for me. The charger housing has four built-in charging cables (two USB-C, one Lightning, one USB-A), plus three additional independent ports, allowing you to charge six devices simultaneously without bringing extra cables, making packing much easier.']

['USB-C ports support 20W fast charging, and BLAVOR says a standard iPhone can be fully charged in about 50 minutes (the situation for the Pro and Pro Max will naturally be different). In terms of capacity, the 20000mAh can charge an iPhone 17 approximately 4 times, an iPad mini about 2.7 times, and an Apple Watch about 37 times. These figures are provided by BLAVOR, but for a charger of this capacity, the numbers are roughly reasonable. Actual performance depends heavily on factors such as ambient temperature and whether the device is in use at the same time.']

['Supports wireless charging, but not MagSafe']

['The top of the charger has a wireless charging area for iPhone and Apple Watch, but it lacks magnetic attachment. This is the standard Qi protocol, not MagSafe or Qi2, so your iPhone can only lie flat on the charging pad and will not attach automatically. If you place the charger on a table, the iPhone can rest stably while charging; however, if placed in a bag, it may not maintain a connection. It would be ideal if future models could incorporate MagSafe.']

['BLAVOR only indicates that the wired USB-C ports support 20W output, so the wireless charging pad is only suitable as a supplementary charging method, not a primary charging solution. If you want to charge at the fastest speed, you should use the four cables that are already connected to the charger.']

["Solar charging is a nice addition, but you can't rely on it to charge the battery from zero to full. A solar panel this small, no matter how long it sits in the sun, cannot fully charge a 20000mAh battery in a single day. However, it can prevent the charger from running completely out of power during long trips and provide support in emergencies where there are no outlets. I would treat it as a backup option."]

['BLAVOR includes seven accessories in the package, including a flashlight with three modes, a camping lantern with three brightness levels, a compass, a thermometer, a carabiner, and a lanyard. It has an IPX5 waterproof rating, which can withstand splashes and rain.']

['Conclusion']

["If you're flying, this charger might not be your top choice. But it is quite suitable for activities like camping and tailgating. It offers a wealth of wired charging options and can supplement power via solar energy in emergencies; the concept is quite unique. I would put it in my camping backpack."]

['You can purchase the BLAVOR Solar Charger directly from Amazon or the BLAVOR official website.']
